topic.ARCHIVAR.extra 2.label: Lending rules
topic.ARCHIVAR.extra 2.001: Can I borrow anything from here to take home?
topic.ARCHIVAR.extra 2.002: The lending rules, article three: originals do not leave the reading room. Copies do.
topic.ARCHIVAR.extra 2.003: And if I lose a copy?
topic.ARCHIVAR.extra 2.004: We make a new one. That’s exactly what a copy is for – being lost.
topic.ARCHIVAR.extra 2.005: So an original must never be lost.
topic.ARCHIVAR.extra 2.006: Never. That’s why I don’t even lend it to myself.
topic.DEZI.ambient 1.label: What do you pick up?
topic.DEZI.ambient 1.001: People calling out into the world and asking whether anyone can hear them.
topic.DEZI.ambient 1.002: A network like that could have a future.
topic.DEZI.ambient 1.x01: A future? The present without hiss is enough for me. Yesterday a chap from Norway called in and we spent an hour discussing aerials.
topic.DEZI.ambient 1.x03: In English, and with our hands. You can’t see hands over the radio, but they help anyway.
topic.DEZI.ambient 2.label: What does precision mean to you?
topic.DEZI.ambient 2.001: Precise doesn’t mean identical. Precise is when you know why something reads differently.
topic.DEZI.ambient 2.x01: Write it down. Mira once wrote it for me on a bit of cardboard, and it still hangs above my desk.
topic.DEZI.ambient 2.x02: Mrs Hrušková has a rule for everything.
topic.DEZI.ambient 2.x03: And an exception to every one. She writes those smaller, so you have to look for them.
topic.DEZI.extra 1.label: Working with Mira
topic.DEZI.extra 1.001: How did you and Mrs Hrušková meet?
topic.DEZI.extra 1.002: At a radio hams’ meeting. She fixed my power supply before I’d managed to tell her what was wrong with it.
topic.DEZI.extra 1.004: Then we drew that map together. She drew, I held the ruler and explained why it was crooked.
topic.DEZI.extra 1.006: It wasn’t. I just needed to explain something.
topic.DEZI.extra 2.label: Call signs
topic.DEZI.extra 2.001: What do those letters and numbers on the wall mean?
topic.DEZI.extra 2.002: Call signs. Every radio ham has one, like an address in the air.
topic.DEZI.extra 2.004: I’m not telling you – you’d be calling me at midnight. The neighbours call me ‘the one with the aerial’.
topic.DEZI.extra 2.006: The most accurate one I have. All of Petržalka knows it.
topic.EMIL.ambient 1.label: What are you playing?
topic.EMIL.ambient 1.001: Whatever I remember. And where I forget, I improvise.
topic.EMIL.ambient 1.002: That’s how I write my service reports too.
topic.EMIL.ambient 1.x02: Not as long as it works.
topic.EMIL.ambient 1.x03: That’s my rule as well. As long as it plays, nobody wants to see the music.
topic.EMIL.ambient 2.label: Who listens to you?
topic.EMIL.ambient 2.001: My most faithful listener is a lady who waits every day for the tram going the other way.
topic.EMIL.ambient 2.002: Maybe she picked her stop by the programme.
topic.EMIL.ambient 2.x01: Maybe. Twice now she’s missed her tram before I finished.
topic.EMIL.ambient 2.x03: No. She waited for the next one and dropped a crown in my cup. For the extended version, she said.
topic.EMIL.extra 1.label: Karlova Ves
topic.EMIL.extra 1.001: Why do you play in Karlova Ves of all places?
topic.EMIL.extra 1.002: Because the trams pull in slowly here. People have time to hear at least the chorus.
topic.EMIL.extra 1.004: In the centre people rush. There I’d only get through the intro and the thank-you.
topic.EMIL.extra 2.label: The accordion
topic.EMIL.extra 2.001: How long have you been playing the accordion?
topic.EMIL.extra 2.002: Since I was ten. My father gave it to me so I wouldn’t run around outside.
topic.EMIL.extra 2.004: No. I ran around outside with the accordion.
topic.FOTO.ambient 1.label: Developing
topic.FOTO.ambient 1.002: I’ll develop a technical shot straight away. Please wait at the dry counter.
topic.FOTO.ambient 1.003: The dry counter? So you don’t wait at the wet one?
topic.FOTO.ambient 1.x01: At the wet one you don’t wait, you soak. And anyone who waits there smells of fixer for a week.
topic.FOTO.ambient 2.label: When is a photo at its best?
topic.FOTO.ambient 2.001: When people think I’ve stopped taking pictures.
topic.FOTO.ambient 2.002: So that click at the end is just theatre.
topic.FOTO.ambient 2.x01: Theatre for the ones who smile on command. The others I photograph when they breathe out.
topic.FOTO.ambient 2.x03: Even now, I would. Only the film for my camera doesn’t arrive until tomorrow.
topic.FOTO.extra 1.label: The darkroom
topic.FOTO.extra 1.001: How long can you stay in the darkroom?
topic.FOTO.extra 1.002: All afternoon. I think better in the dark, because I can’t see the mess.
topic.FOTO.extra 1.003: And you never have to look for anything in there?
topic.FOTO.extra 1.004: No. Everything is in its place. If someone moves something, I find out with my fingers.
topic.FOTO.extra 2.label: School photos
topic.FOTO.extra 2.001: Do you photograph school classes too?
topic.FOTO.extra 2.002: Every June. Thirty children, three rows, and always one who sneezes.
topic.FOTO.extra 2.003: And what do you do about him?
topic.FOTO.extra 2.004: I leave him be. Twenty years later, he’s the main reason everyone looks at that photo.
topic.JANA95.ambient 1.label: Do you help with the club?
topic.JANA95.ambient 1.001: Yes, with the timetable, the paperwork and the room. A club always needs someone to keep things in order.
topic.JANA95.ambient 1.002: And someone who leaves room for new ideas.
topic.JANA95.ambient 1.x01: I have a separate compartment in my binder for ideas. So far it’s the fullest one.
topic.JANA95.ambient 1.x02: Even for the ones that don’t follow the template?
topic.JANA95.ambient 1.x03: Those most of all. The templates are in the cupboard; they don’t need a compartment.
topic.JANA95.extra 2.label: The club’s paperwork
topic.JANA95.extra 2.001: All this paperwork for one club?
topic.JANA95.extra 2.002: Application forms, parents’ consent, the room schedule and one list of who has a key.
topic.JANA95.extra 2.003: But the caretaker has the keys.
topic.JANA95.extra 2.004: The caretaker has the bunch. The list is so we know who has which key from the bunch.
topic.JANA95.extra 1.label: Your work
topic.JANA95.extra 1.001: I can see you’ve got your hands full. What’s it going to be?
topic.JANA95.extra 1.002: An exhibition. The schedule, name cards and the order. Without an order, an exhibition is just a table with things on it.
topic.JANA95.extra 1.003: And what will be on that table?
topic.JANA95.extra 1.004: Radios, a tape recorder and a model mill that only turns when nobody’s looking at it.
topic.JANA95.extra 1.005: I know that one. In my workshop everything works too, until a customer walks in.
topic.JANA95.extra 1.006: The model isn’t for repair. It’s an exhibit, and an exhibit doesn’t have to turn.
topic.JURAJ.ambient 1.label: Why blocks of flats?
topic.JURAJ.ambient 1.001: Everyone looks at them from the outside. I draw the lights in the windows.
topic.JURAJ.ambient 1.002: That’s a much bigger map than it looks.
topic.JURAJ.ambient 1.x01: Bigger. There are two hundred windows in our block alone, and every evening different ones are lit.
topic.JURAJ.ambient 1.x03: Third from the top, on the left. When I’m drawing, Mum leaves the light on so I can find my way home.
topic.JURAJ.ambient 2.label: Have you got permission?
topic.JURAJ.ambient 2.001: Of course. Here, stamp and all.
topic.JURAJ.ambient 2.002: A stamp? For drawing with chalk?
topic.JURAJ.ambient 2.x01: A stamp from the council. And the consent of the lady who washes the steps here.
topic.JURAJ.ambient 2.x03: It’s more important. She’s the one who scrubs the underpass afterwards.
topic.JURAJ.extra 1.label: The windows of Petržalka
topic.JURAJ.extra 1.001: Which window in Petržalka is the most beautiful?
topic.JURAJ.extra 1.002: The one with the light on when everyone else is asleep. Someone in there is reading, or waiting for someone.
topic.JURAJ.extra 1.003: Or forgot to switch it off.
topic.JURAJ.extra 2.label: Why chalk?
topic.JURAJ.extra 2.001: Why do you draw in chalk and not paint?
topic.JURAJ.extra 2.002: Chalk washes off. When someone moves out, I switch off their window with a cloth.
topic.JURAJ.extra 2.004: It isn’t. A month later someone moves in, and I light their window up again.
topic.JURO.ambient 1.label: Why cassettes?
topic.JURO.ambient 1.001: They have a side A and a side B. At least they admit there are two sides to everything.
topic.JURO.ambient 1.x01: And when the tape gets tangled, a pencil’s all you need. Don’t try that with other technology.
topic.JURO.ambient 1.x03: A record. Take a pencil to that and you’ll scratch the whole of side A.
topic.JURO.ambient 2.label: Does hiss bother you?
topic.JURO.ambient 2.001: A bit of hiss doesn’t matter. What matters is throwing away a whole song because of it.
topic.JURO.ambient 2.002: I’ll remember that. One day I’ll need to tell someone.
topic.JURO.ambient 2.x01: Then play them the song first. Maybe they’ll start humming along and forget the hiss.
topic.JURO.extra 1.label: Your best cassette
topic.JURO.extra 1.002: The one without a label. One night in ninety-three I recorded the radio on it, and to this day I don’t know what’s on it.
topic.JURO.extra 1.003: Why don’t you find out what’s on it and label it?
topic.JURO.extra 1.004: Because if I knew what was on it, I’d stop listening to it. This way it still tempts me.
topic.JURO.extra 2.label: A club in the basement
topic.JURO.extra 2.001: Why is the club in the basement?
topic.JURO.extra 2.002: Because you can’t hear the trams down here. And the neighbours can’t hear us.
topic.JURO.extra 2.004: More of a ceasefire. An agreement would be if we’d ever talked about it on the stairs.
topic.KUBO.extra 1.label: First year
topic.KUBO.extra 1.001: What year are you in at school?
topic.KUBO.extra 1.002: First. I can already read, write and whistle through my fingers.
topic.KUBO.extra 1.003: And which of those did they teach you at school?
topic.KUBO.extra 1.004: Reading and writing. My brother taught me to whistle, but that doesn’t go on your report.
topic.KUBO.extra 1.005: Shame. You’d get top marks for it.
topic.KUBO.extra 1.006: Miss wouldn’t give me top marks. She’s heard my whistling.
topic.KUBO.extra 2.label: Why is there such a big wall here?
topic.KUBO.extra 2.001: Why is there such a high wall round the playground?
topic.KUBO.extra 2.002: So the ball doesn’t run into the street. But it runs off anyway, just higher.
topic.KUBO.extra 2.003: And who goes and gets it?
topic.KUBO.extra 2.005: When the ball lands on the balcony on the fourth floor, the lady throws it back. But first she tells us how many geraniums we’ve broken.
topic.KUBO.extra 2.007: All of them. But she’s got lots.
topic.KUBO.extra 3.label: The bell rings
topic.KUBO.extra 3.001: So, how’s riding with a bell?
topic.KUBO.extra 3.002: Faster. When I ring, everyone gets out of the way, even the pigeons.
topic.KUBO.extra 3.003: And the lady on the fourth floor?
topic.KUBO.extra 3.004: Not her. She rings back at us from her balcony, with a spoon on a saucepan.
topic.LEA95.ambient 1.label: What should the children record?
topic.LEA95.ambient 1.001: Anything they’d like to remember. Even if it seems silly to them today.
topic.LEA95.ambient 1.x01: And what have they recorded so far?
topic.LEA95.ambient 1.x02: The bell for break, a dripping tap, a man feeding the pigeons and one sneeze.
topic.LEA95.ambient 1.x03: They apologised for that sneeze all week. It’s the best thing on the tape.
topic.LEA95.ambient 2.label: Do you record silence too?
topic.LEA95.ambient 2.001: Even the pauses between words. That’s when people think.
topic.LEA95.ambient 2.002: Mine would fill a cassette of their own.
topic.LEA95.ambient 2.x01: Then let it have its own. Little Adam from the club stays quiet the longest of them all too.
topic.LEA95.ambient 2.x02: And what does he say afterwards?
topic.LEA95.after.label: ‘Never Fear, Darling’?
topic.LEA95.after.001: Mira once brought back a programme from Ivanka for a play called ‘Never Fear, Darling!’ The children still laugh at that title.
topic.LEA95.after.002: The programme survived. Does anyone still perform the play?
topic.LEA95.after.x01: One boy wants to record it as a radio play. All the parts himself.
topic.LEA95.after.x02: And has he got the script?
topic.LEA95.after.x03: Only the first line so far. But he performs it brilliantly.
topic.LEA95.extra 1.label: The most beautiful sound
topic.LEA95.extra 1.001: Which sound do you like best of all?
topic.LEA95.extra 1.002: When the bell has gone and the children sit on for a moment, and nobody knows who’ll get up first.
topic.LEA95.extra 1.004: Not quite. There are thirty people in it, all making up their minds.
topic.LEA95.extra 2.label: Your children
topic.LEA95.extra 2.001: Do you have children of your own, or are these enough for you?
topic.LEA95.extra 2.002: I have a son, Viktor. He’s ten, like some of these.
topic.LEA95.extra 2.003: And what does he like doing?
topic.LEA95.extra 2.004: At home he takes apart everything that has a screw in it. He wants to know how it works.
topic.LEA95.extra 2.005: And does he put it back together?
topic.LEA95.extra 2.006: Not yet. But he puts every part carefully away in a little box.
topic.MILADA.ambient 1.label: What’s hardest to mend?
topic.MILADA.ambient 1.001: The phrase ‘it’s always been like that’.
topic.MILADA.ambient 1.002: I know that one. Today more than ever.
topic.MILADA.ambient 1.x01: With a coat, you just unpick and sew. With a phrase like that, you first have to convince whoever’s wearing it.
topic.MILADA.ambient 1.x03: Now and then. Usually when the coat starts getting tight on them.
topic.MILADA.ambient 2.label: Do you know about cables too?
topic.MILADA.ambient 2.001: A cable needs a good coat too.
topic.MILADA.ambient 2.002: Especially when it doesn’t want to touch the others.
topic.MILADA.ambient 2.x01: The first cable I sewed a cover for was a neighbour’s guitar lead. The guitar still plays; the neighbour learned two chords.
topic.MILADA.ambient 2.x02: Two chords will get you through half the songs there are.
topic.MILADA.ambient 2.x03: He tells me that under my window every summer.
topic.MILADA.extra 1.label: Ružinov
topic.MILADA.extra 1.001: How long have you had your shop in Ružinov?
topic.MILADA.extra 1.002: Eighteen years. First I mended trousers; now I mend decisions made at the market too.
topic.MILADA.extra 1.004: At Miletička everyone buys trousers a size too small, because they were cheaper. Then they come to me.
topic.MILADA.extra 2.label: June at the tailor’s
topic.MILADA.extra 2.001: Who comes to you most often?
topic.MILADA.extra 2.002: Mums, just before the end of the school year. In June every pair of trousers rips.
topic.MILADA.extra 2.004: Because in June children climb trees. In September they’re back sitting at their desks.
topic.MIRA95.ambient 1.label: Why record a school?
topic.MIRA95.ambient 1.001: People photograph buildings. But in twenty years nobody will know what break time sounded like.
topic.MIRA95.ambient 1.002: I can still hear it today.
topic.MIRA95.ambient 1.003: Then you know why we do it.
topic.MIRA95.ambient 1.x01: And what does break time sound like in ninety-five?
topic.MIRA95.ambient 1.x02: First the bell, then thirty chairs at once, then someone running down the corridor even though it isn’t allowed.
topic.MIRA95.ambient 1.x03: We’ve got more recordings of that last one than anything else.
topic.MIRA95.ambient 2.label: Do we know each other?
topic.MIRA95.ambient 2.001: You hold a screwdriver in an odd way. I know someone like that.
topic.MIRA95.ambient 2.003: Then don’t fix it. It works.
topic.MIRA95.ambient 2.x02: I’m not telling you. You’d start copying him.
topic.MIRA95.after.label: Has anything changed?
topic.MIRA95.after.001: The old register has the full storage number again. You put something right.
topic.MIRA95.after.002: More like I just didn’t let what was right get lost.
topic.MIRA95.after.003: That tends to be the better repair.
topic.MIRA95.after.x01: I’ll write it down anyway. Z-17 goes in the register, and in my notebook, that someone helped.
topic.MIRA95.after.x03: I’ll add the name once I’m sure. I never write anything in advance.
topic.MIRA95.extra 1.label: The sound club
topic.MIRA95.extra 1.001: How did you come up with the idea of running a sound club?
topic.MIRA95.extra 1.002: At first I wanted to teach the children to solder. Then I found out what they like best is listening.
topic.MIRA95.extra 1.003: So you gave up on soldering?
topic.MIRA95.extra 1.004: I didn’t give it up, I just moved it to second place. Listen first, then take apart and solder.
topic.MIRA95.extra 2.label: Cassettes in the cupboard
topic.MIRA95.extra 2.001: How many cassettes have you recorded so far?
topic.MIRA95.extra 2.002: Forty-seven. Each one has a label: the date, the class and one word saying what it’s about.
topic.MIRA95.extra 2.004: It has to be. Anyone who can’t say it in one word goes back and listens again. Nobody gets a bigger label.
topic.MIRA95.extra 3.label: Dúbravka these days
topic.MIRA95.extra 3.001: What’s life like in Dúbravka these days?
topic.MIRA95.extra 3.002: Fast. Where there was a shop there’s a kiosk, and where there was a kiosk there’s a shop again. I can hardly keep changing my way to the shops.
topic.MIRA95.extra 3.004: The club is the only thing here that always starts at three. I insist on that.
topic.PALI.ambient 1.label: The guarantee
topic.PALI.ambient 1.001: What sort of guarantee do you give?
topic.PALI.ambient 1.002: That I’ll tell you the truth when a repair isn’t worth it.
topic.PALI.ambient 1.003: And how many people have you told that today?
topic.PALI.ambient 1.x01: Two. Both left annoyed, and one came back with something better to repair.
topic.PALI.ambient 1.x03: It pays. Just not straight away.
topic.PALI.ambient 2.label: What will happen to technology?
topic.PALI.ambient 2.001: It’ll get smaller. But screws won’t disappear.
topic.PALI.ambient 2.003: We don’t use words like that in here.
topic.PALI.ambient 2.x02: And I hope it never does. Glue belongs in a stationer’s, not a repair shop.
topic.PALI.extra 1.label: Your worst repair
topic.PALI.extra 1.002: A radio that only picked up one station. The customer swore it was working yesterday.
topic.PALI.extra 1.003: And what was wrong with it?
topic.PALI.extra 1.004: Nothing. His dog had eaten the tuning knob.
topic.PALI.extra 1.006: He still listens to it. Says he’s got used to it.
topic.PALI.extra 2.label: Drive belts
topic.PALI.extra 2.001: How many drive belts have you actually got here?
topic.PALI.extra 2.002: Three drawers. Round ones, flat ones and the ones that look like hair ties.
topic.PALI.extra 2.003: And can you tell them apart?
topic.PALI.extra 2.004: I can. My daughter once took one for her plait and stretched it. The neighbour’s tape recorder sang bass with it afterwards.
topic.SONA.ambient 1.label: Who won?
